newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off in thin volume on U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off in thin volume on U.S. rates.

text.p: Brazil stocks fell for a third day in a row Monday, ending 1.98 percent lower amid concerns about U.S. interest rates and lingering worries that Brazil's Central Bank may close several brokerages, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares closed off at 12,017 points. Volume was lower than usual at 723.6 million reais ($670 million).

Analysts said the Sao Paulo bolsa closed lower even though Wall Street stocks managed to end slightly higher after trading in negative territory most of the session amid fears that U.S. inflation concerns might prompt higher rates there.
Traders said that continued concerns that Brazil's Central Bank may shut down brokerages contributed to slow trading and depress share prices.
"The market always loses liquidity in a situation like that," said one analyst.

On Friday, the Sao Paulo bolsa closed sharply lower following an unconfirmed report that the government planned to release a list of brokerages it would liquidate after a Central Bank investigation on an alleged multi-million dollar scam involving state and municipal debt.
Traders also said that fears that other brokerages may suffer liquidation could help fueling speculation ahead of mid-August futures and options expiry.
Futures index contracts are due to settle on August 13, while the options will settle on August 18, they added.

Bellwether Telebras preferred dropped 2.63 percent to close at 148 reais, despite reports by a number of banks and brokerages reiterating their buy recommendations on the stock following the firm's first half results.
Federal power utility Eletrobras preferred fell 1.67 percent to 590 reais, contributing to a 2.11 percent drop in the power sector index to 3,412 points.
State oil firm Petrobras ended flat at 310.01 reais, while privatized mining giant CVRD rose a slight 0.29 percent to end at 28 reais.
Brokers said market could continue weak Tuesday amid low liquidity.
